title: Two Sum
summary: Practice trading a little extra memory for a faster search through a sequence.

prompt.description: Write a function that finds two different positions in an integer list whose values add up to a given target. Return the positions in either order, and assume one valid pair exists.

examples.explanation: The values at positions 1 and 3 total 8.
The values at positions 0 and 2 total 2.

constraints: The list contains at least two integers.
Do not use the same position twice.
Aim for better than checking every pair when possible.

title: Valid Parentheses
summary: Use a last-in-first-out structure to reason about nested delimiters.

prompt.description: Given a string made only of bracket characters, decide whether every opening bracket is closed by the matching type in the correct nested order.

examples.explanation: Each pair closes in reverse order of opening.
The closing bracket types do not match the nesting order.

constraints: The input contains only (), [], and {} characters.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
summary: Track a running opportunity while scanning time-ordered values once.

prompt.description: Given daily prices for one asset, choose one day to buy and a later day to sell. Return the largest positive gain, or zero if no profitable trade is possible.

examples.explanation: Buying at 2 and selling later at 10 gives a gain of 8.
Every later price is lower than the earlier prices.

constraints: There is at least one recorded day.
The buy day must come before the sell day.

title: Binary Search
summary: Narrow a sorted search space by repeatedly choosing a midpoint.

prompt.description: Create a function that locates a target in an ascending integer list. Return its position when present, or -1 when the target is absent.

examples.explanation: The target is stored at position 3.
The target does not occur in the list.

constraints: The input list is sorted in ascending order.

title: Merge Intervals
summary: Order ranges and combine neighboring spans when their boundaries overlap.

prompt.description: Given a collection of numeric ranges, combine ranges that share any values and return the resulting non-overlapping ranges in ascending order.

examples.explanation: The first two ranges overlap and form one range.
The ranges are separate and are returned in order.

constraints: Each range has a start no greater than its end.
Input ranges may be in any order.
